title: Cyrus and the Parish
premise: True-crime podcaster Paloma Okafor arrives in the coastal parish of St. Brannoc to reopen the 1994 disappearance of a teenage girl, Verity Tresidder, whose body was never found. When a fresh corpse washes up wearing clothes stolen from Paloma's own closet, it becomes clear someone in the parish knows she's closing in — and wants her to stop. As Paloma untangles alibis woven thirty years ago by the parish's most powerful family, they discover Verity's death was covered up by the man who now runs the town, and that the killer's accomplice has been leaving them clues out of guilt and love. In the end, the tide gives up Verity's remains, the patriarch is exposed in a public confrontation at the parish church, and Paloma — who grew up in care and never belonged anywhere — chooses to stay, finding belonging in the community they helped free.
about_author: Astrid Marchetti is the pen name of a former investigative journalist who spent a decade covering cold cases along the English coast before turning to fiction. She lives in a converted chapel with her dog, Brixham, and an unhealthy collection of tide tables.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Paloma Okafor arrives in St. Brannoc to record the pilot episode on Verity Tresidder's 1994 disappearance, interviewing the girl's aging mother, Edith. POV: Paloma. The beat is wary curiosity — Paloma senses the parish's polite warmth has a locked door behind it, and Edith slips her a key: 'Ask about the regatta night.'

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: A body washes up at Gull Rock wearing Paloma's own stolen jacket and scarf, making them a suspect and a target. Detective Sergeant Ruan Pascoe, hostile but honest, shares the forensics off the record. POV: Paloma. The emotional beat is violated exposure — the killer has studied them, and Paloma realizes this isn't a warning; it's an invitation.

chapters.title: The Regatta Alibi
chapters.summary: Paloma reconstructs regatta night 1994 through old recordings: five witnesses, five matching stories, too perfect by half. All roads lead to Aldous Penhale, the parish's patriarch and then-harbourmaster. POV: alternating Paloma and DS Pascoe. The beat is mounting dread as the seamless alibi reveals itself as choreography, not truth.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Edith dies suddenly — officially a fall — hours after telling Paloma she'd found Verity's diary. POV: Paloma, grieving and furious. The beat is loss hardening into resolve; Paloma stops being an observer of the case and becomes part of it, recording Edith's last words as both evidence and elegy.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Anonymous audio files arrive at the podcast inbox: a woman's voice, whispering fragments of regatta night. Paloma identifies her as Meraud Penhale, Aldous's wife, once Verity's confidante. POV: Paloma. The beat is uneasy alliance — love against duty taking shape, as Meraud betrays her husband in whispers she can't yet speak aloud.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Meraud's fragmented testimony, cross-checked against harbour logs, cracks the alibi: Verity was alive at midnight, not ten o'clock as all five witnesses claimed. POV: Meraud, in flashback-laced present. The beat is guilt surfacing like a drowned thing — she saw something that night and chose the parish over the girl.

chapters.title: A House Built on Water
chapters.summary: Paloma confronts Aldous at Penhale House under the pretext of an interview; he deflects with charm, then menace, revealing he knows about Meraud's messages. POV: Paloma. The beat is power showing its teeth — Aldous doesn't deny anything, he simply explains what happens to people who dig in his parish.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Meraud gives Paloma a full recorded confession: she helped move Verity's body to protect her son, Jago, then seventeen, who killed Verity in panic after she threatened to expose their affair. POV: Meraud. The beat is devastating tenderness — a mother's love weaponized into complicity, thirty years of rot from one act of protection.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Storm surge exposes remains beneath the old slipway; Jago, now the harbourside developer, tries to destroy Meraud's tape and silence Paloma, but Pascoe arrests him mid-act. POV: Paloma and Pascoe converging. The climax beat is collision — duty finally outweighs blood, and the parish watches its heir led away past the water that kept its secret.

chapters.title: Parish
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Verity is buried beside Edith; Aldous resigns in disgrace, and the podcast finale airs the whole truth. Meraud faces charges but finds unexpected mercy from the town. POV: Paloma. The resolution beat is belonging — offered a book deal in London, Paloma instead signs a lease above the chandlery, finally home in the place they came to unbury.
